checks.name: matcher — complete season RSC
checks.note: Must remain non-empty; typed extraction is covered by provider replay tests.

checks.name: api/game — live shape (first-period capture 2026-09-18)
checks.note: The sample is the in-play document; live the same route answers whatever state the game is in now. currentPeriodStart is null outside play and the tool counts a null as absent, so it is left to the sample comparison rather than required here.

checks.name: api/games — several games by document id
games/{slug}/view — game page RSC with lineups
checks.note: Must stay non-empty and carry "homeLineups"; the typed extraction is covered by the provider replay test

checks.name: pages/tabell - page still answers (standings moved out of it 2026-09-25)
checks.note: The page used to server-render a stats.league-standings component with all 14 rows; on 2026-09-25 it became a client-rendered shell and the rows moved to POST /api/league-standings-all-time. Kept as a plain liveness check so a move back, or the page disappearing, is both visible.

checks.name: players/{slug} - player profile RSC
checks.note: A retired or transferred player keeps his page; an unknown slug answers 200 with the not-found page, so this check proves reachability only.

checks.name: api/all-players - a club's squad (POST)
checks.note: Keyed by the CMS short name (MoDo), not the StatNet id (MODO): the wrong one answers 200 with an empty list, so a silent drift here would look like a club with no squad. A read behind POST, which is why this check needs one.

checks.name: api/all-players - the wrong club code is an empty 200 (POST)
checks.note: Pins the failure mode itself: the StatNet id is not the squad route's key and never errors when used as one. If this ever starts returning players, the two code systems have been merged upstream.

checks.name: api/player-leaderboard - a club's scorers (POST)
checks.note: Keyed by the StatNet id here, the opposite of the squad route. Omitting phase empties the answer with no error, so the body is pinned whole.

checks.name: api/team-leaderboard - shots on goal (POST)
checks.note: SOG and SVSPerc are the only two columns the standings row has not got, which is the whole reason this route is called.

checks.name: api/play-by-play - a finished game (POST)
checks.note: All four body fields are required (a missing one is a 400); playedDateTime, which the site sends, is not. Only statNetGameNumber selects the game. The server proxies StatNet, which answered one call in three under opening-night load, so a fail here can be upstream rather than drift.

checks.name: api/play-by-play - a game StatNet has no sheet for (POST)
checks.note: All four fields are required - omitting any gives 400 "Missing required fields" - but only statNetGameNumber selects the game: a wrong scheduledDateTime or side id still answers the right one. An unknown number is what 404s, and that is also what a fixture before its opening face-off answers, which the provider reads as "no events yet" rather than a failure.

checks.name: api/league-standings-all-time - the table (POST)
checks.note: Where the league table went when /pages/tabell stopped server-rendering it. No StatNet id on a row any more, only the display code, so the core joins through the season snapshot; power_play_perc and penalty_kill_perc are empty strings in every season seen and come from the team leaderboard instead.

checks.name: api/league-standings-all-time - a finished season (POST)
checks.note: The one thing the old page could not do: it ignored every season parameter. 2025-26 is finished, so this check is stable - 52 games and IF Bjorkloven on 119 points.

checks.name: api/team-leaderboard - power play (POST)
checks.note: PP% and PK% are no longer on a standings row, so these two calls are what the table's special-teams columns are made of. The route takes no season: current only.
